source_title: Rockstar Games Issues New Official Statement on GTA 6's Open World - GameRant
source_excerpt:
GTA 6 is less than a month away, and Rockstar Games has made some enormous promises about what players can expect from its return to Vice City. The upcoming open-world game is larger than GTA 5 , but it's not just the size of the open world. Rockstar believes the company has taken a giant step forward in making a world feel lived-in, but also making the story work hand-in-hand with the open world (which conflicts in a lot of games).
Of course, one of the defining features of GTA 5 and Red Dead Redemption 2 is the freedom to ignore the main story and simply explore. Rockstar's worlds have always encouraged experimentation and exploration, and GTA 6 is no different. GTA 6 is building on that philosophy, although its two protagonists, Jason and Lucia, introduce another layer to the experience. Instead of simply moving through Leonida alone, players can spend time with their partner and potentially discover opportunities they wouldn't have encountered otherwise.
Rockstar on Balancing GTA 6's Story and Open-World Gameplay
gta 6 fishing gameplay Image via Rockstar Games
Speaking with IGN , Rockstar's Rob Nelson described GTA 6 as a significant improvement in open-world gameplay , world size, population density, and NPC interactions, suggesting that the difference becomes obvious once players begin exploring Vice City. Nelson specifically highlighted the number of vehicles and pedestrians populating the world, along with the ways those characters respond to players:
"It is definitely a step forward in all respects for us: the size of the world and how deep it feels. It’s a bit of a shock when you get in there, and you see the density of the traffic, the density of population, and the fidelity of their responses to you."
However, Rockstar wants to give GTA 6 players more than a bigger playground. Nelson also discussed the challenge of balancing GTA 6 's open-world freedom with a compelling narrative, acknowledging that certain story moments require more guidance than others. While that approach isn't going away, Rockstar has deliberately worked to give players more freedom whenever possible. Narrative takes the fore sometimes, but most of the time, GTA 6 's story and open world work together to tell a specific tale (which is largely still under wraps). As Nelson said,
"We are always trying to find that balance between freedom and storytelling. It is a challenge, and sometimes when you are trying to create a specific or hopefully compelling narrative, the narrative aspect does need to take precedence at times—at least for us it does. To move the narrative forward in a believable way, you have to hit these beats, and so in those cases, we have to kind of guide the experience. But with this game, we have made a very conscious effort to open things up where possible – without compromising the quality of the experience."
One particularly interesting example, given during IGN's preview, of GTA 6's reactive world involves Jason suggesting an activity that even Nelson hadn't previously encountered. During a gameplay session, Nelson was driving toward a pawn shop when Jason spotted a car park and suggested another job. The unexpected dialogue convinced Nelson to abandon his original plans, demonstrating how the game's characters can introduce new opportunities for ordinary exploration.
"We are very excited about some of what we have going on now in the open world, with how it reacts to you and the systems we have working together. We have a lot of emergent natural-feeling stuff happening pretty often now as you roam around the world. That was truly emergent for me, when we drove past that car park and Jason suggested we do that job – I hadn’t actually heard that dialogue from him myself yet. And it worked – I was going to a pawn shop, then Jason said, ‘Should we go do this?’ as we drove by, and I changed my mind.
These kinds of spontaneous interactions could make GTA 6 feel considerably less predictable, especially when players are simply driving around Vice City without a specific objective. That said, the objective on GTA 6 's release date on November 19 is going to be taking in everything Rockstar has to offer.
